action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the source or assigned by the analyst expressed on a source-specific numeric scale. This score provides finer-grained confidence information than the categorical confidence_id value. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should reflect the the same assessment as confidence if both are populated.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.caption: Alert
is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

risk_details.caption: Risk Details
risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

osint.caption: OSINT
osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Identity & Access Management.

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Authentication.

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.caption: Enrichments
enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

message.caption: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

raw_data.caption: Raw Data
raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.caption: Raw Data Hash
raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.caption: Raw Data Size
raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description:
The details about the authentication request. For example, possible details for Windows logon or logoff events are:
  • Success
    • LOGOFF_USER_INITIATED
    • LOGOFF_OTHER
  • Failure
    • USER_DOES_NOT_EXIST
    • INVALID_CREDENTIALS
    • ACCOUNT_DISABLED
    • ACCOUNT_LOCKED_OUT
    • PASSWORD_EXPIRED

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that performed this operation. Carries model identity via ai_agent.ai_model. Populate when the action was performed by an agent rather than a direct model call.

ai_capability.caption: AI Capability
ai_capability.description: The AI capability invoked in this operation: a tool, resource, or prompt, in the sense of the MCP primitives. Records the capability's identity, kind, provenance, declared contracts, and declared safety hints. Transport details remain on the event's transport attributes (e.g., api, http_request), and affected objects remain in resources. Producers deriving activity_id from the capability's declared hints (e.g., mapping a declared read-only tool to Read) should note the hints are self-declared and unverified; when the observed operation contradicts the declaration, classify by observed behavior.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model involved in this operation. Use for direct model invocations where no autonomous agent is involved. For agent-mediated operations, model identity is carried within ai_agent.ai_model instead.

delegation.caption: Delegation
delegation.description: The delegation under whose authority this AI operation was performed. Links the event to a durable authorization context independent of traces and sessions, enabling correlation of all events executed under the same delegated authority.

message_context.caption: Message Context
message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.

ai_status.caption: AI Status
ai_status.description: Per-operation outcome scalars for this operation, such as the stop reason and the permission check result, grouped in the ai_status object so they do not proliferate as discrete attributes at the event root. Additional outcome attributes may be added to the object in later versions.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Details about the underlying HTTP request.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Details about the underlying HTTP response.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Details about the source of the IAM activity.

account_switch_type.caption: Account Switch Type
account_switch_type.description: The account switch method, normalized to the caption of the account_switch_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

account_switch_type_id.caption: Account Switch Type ID
account_switch_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the account switch method.

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: Describes a category of methods used for identity verification in an authentication attempt.

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authentication protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authentication protocol used to create the user session.

authentication_token.caption: Authentication Token
authentication_token.description: The authentication token, ticket, or assertion, e.g. Kerberos, OIDC, SAML.

certificate.caption: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate associated with the authentication or pre-authentication (Kerberos).

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: The endpoint to which the authentication was targeted.

is_cleartext.caption: Cleartext Credentials
is_cleartext.description:
Indicates whether the credentials were passed in clear text.

Note: True if the credentials were passed in a clear text protocol such as FTP or TELNET, or if Windows detected that a user's logon password was passed to the authentication package in clear text.

is_mfa.caption: Multi Factor Authentication
is_mfa.description: Indicates whether Multi Factor Authentication was used during authentication.

is_new_logon.caption: New Logon
is_new_logon.description: Indicates logon is from a device not seen before or a first time account logon.

is_remote.caption: Remote
is_remote.description: The attempted authentication is over a remote connection.

logon_process.caption: Logon Process
logon_process.description: The trusted process that validated the authentication credentials.

logon_type.caption: Logon Type
logon_type.description: The logon type, normalized to the caption of the logon_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The service or gateway to which the user or process is being authenticated

session.caption: Session
session.description: The authenticated user or service session.

user.caption: User
user.description: The subject (user/role or account) to authenticate.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

time_dt.caption: Event Time
time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

app_name.caption: Application Name
app_name.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process if present.

app_uid.caption: Application ID
app_uid.description: The unique identifier of the client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process.pid or process.uid if present.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that application is distinct from the process if present.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The actor's role, or as an alternative to user or process when the role is serving as a security principal for the operation that initiated the activity.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: This object describes details about the Identity Provider used.

invoked_by.caption: Invoked by
invoked_by.description: The name of the service that invoked the activity as described in the event.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The process that initiated the activity.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session from which the activity was initiated.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that initiated the activity or the user context from which the activity was initiated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for the agent. For example: Q4 Analysis Agent or Model Tester Agent.

uid.caption: AI Agent ID
uid.description: The stable logical identifier for the agent, assigned by the agent's authoritative source (e.g., its control plane, registry, or issuing identity provider). Persists across restarts and instances. Producers populate this from whatever identity they observe: for a runtime that owns the agent, this is its issued ID; for a gateway or proxy, it is typically derived from the agent's credential. Multiple producers logging the same agent should converge on the same uid when they share an authoritative source.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model backing this agent at the time of the recorded event. An agent's model may change across instances or versions; this captures the model in use for the specific logged activity or delegation.

charter.caption: Agent Charter
charter.description: A document that defines an AI agent's durable role, responsibilities, constraints, and operating boundaries. When available, populate hashes on the file for content integrity and signatures for provenance. Integrity of the event that reports this agent is provided separately by the record_integrity profile.

instance_uid.caption: AI Agent Instance ID
instance_uid.description: Identifier for a specific running instance or session of the agent, distinct from the stable logical uid. An instance is a single materialization of the agent: a conversation, session, or run. It may persist across restarts (a session that is suspended and later resumed keeps the same instance_uid) and may span multiple cooperating runtime components, so several events can share one instance_uid. Enables attribution of actions to a particular instance of the agent rather than to the agent generally.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The agent framework, normalized to the caption of the type_id value.

type_id.caption: Agent Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the agent framework. Different agent frameworks have different identity, tool-call, and delegation semantics, so recording the framework enables cross-framework normalization. Communication protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) are a property of individual operations rather than the agent itself, and are surfaced on the relevant operation rather than here.

version.caption: AI Agent Version
version.description: The version of the agent: the agent's own code or configuration revision (e.g., 1.4.2), distinct from the version of the model backing it (carried on ai_model.version). Enables correlation of behavioral changes with charter or configuration revisions across agent versions.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the capability as advertised by its provider: the MCP tool, resource, or prompt name, the function name of a framework-native tool, or the identifier of a built-in tool. For example: get_weather.

uid.caption: AI Capability ID
uid.description: The stable identifier of the capability itself, when one exists: a registry or catalog identifier, or a producer-derived stable key (e.g., serving server identity plus capability name). Identifies the capability across invocations; per-invocation correlation is carried by transaction_uid instead.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

baseline_fingerprint.caption: Baseline Fingerprint
baseline_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the capability's declared contract as recorded at registration or approval time, identifying the approved contract version without embedding the contract body in the event. Compared against the contract fingerprints presented at invocation to detect a declared contract that changed after approval, such as supply-chain "rug pull" changes. Carries the approved value rather than a match verdict; consumers diff, the object does not assess.

cache_scope.caption: Cache Scope
cache_scope.description: The declared cache scope, normalized to the caption of cache_scope_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

cache_scope_id.caption: Cache Scope ID
cache_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the cache scope the serving system declared for this capability's results, modeled on the MCP cacheScope field (itself modeled on HTTP Cache-Control). Determines whether shared intermediaries may cache the result - a data-exposure signal: a Private result cached in a shared scope is a cross-user exposure. Note this is declared caching metadata observed on the serving response, not an invariant property of the capability itself.

cache_ttl.caption: Cache TTL
cache_ttl.description: The declared freshness window for this capability's results, in milliseconds, per the MCP ttlMs field. Bounds how long a cached result was treated as valid by the consuming system.

desc_fingerprint.caption: Description Fingerprint
desc_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the capability's declared natural-language description or instructions (e.g., the tool docstring or manifest description presented at discovery), identifying the description version without embedding the description body in the event. The object carries no desc attribute; this fingerprints the model-visible description by reference. Enables detecting description poisoning, where the description is altered without any schema change.

input_schema_fingerprint.caption: Input Schema Fingerprint
input_schema_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the capability's declared input contract (e.g., its JSON Schema), identifying the contract version without embedding the schema body in the event. Enables grouping by tool-contract version and detecting contract drift, including "rug pull" changes where a tool's schema changes after initial approval. Use serialization_id: JCS when the fingerprint is computed over canonicalized JSON.

is_destructive.caption: Destructive
is_destructive.description: Indicates the capability declared that it may perform destructive updates, per the MCP destructiveHint tool annotation. This is a self-declared, unverified hint from the serving system: it supports triage and pivoting but must not be treated as an enforced property.

is_idempotent.caption: Idempotent
is_idempotent.description: Indicates the capability declared that repeated calls with the same arguments have no additional effect, per the MCP idempotentHint tool annotation. This is a self-declared, unverified hint from the serving system.

is_open_world.caption: Open World
is_open_world.description: Indicates the capability declared that it may interact with an open world of external entities (e.g., the web), rather than a closed domain, per the MCP openWorldHint tool annotation. This is a self-declared, unverified hint from the serving system.

is_readonly.caption: Read-Only
is_readonly.description: Indicates the capability declared that it does not modify its environment, per the MCP readOnlyHint tool annotation. This is a self-declared, unverified hint from the serving system: it supports triage and pivoting (e.g., "every write-capable tool an agent invoked") but must not be treated as an enforced property, and a mismatch between this hint and observed behavior is itself a signal.

mime_type.caption: MIME type
mime_type.description: The declared MIME type of the capability's content. Primarily for Resource primitives, e.g. text/markdown or application/json.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace or grouping the capability belongs to, when the provider organizes capabilities into named collections. For example: weather.

output_schema_fingerprint.caption: Output Schema Fingerprint
output_schema_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the capability's declared structured-output contract, identifying the contract version without embedding the schema body in the event. Use serialization_id: JCS when the fingerprint is computed over canonicalized JSON.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The logical serving system that advertised and served the capability - for MCP, the MCP server. This is provenance, not a network endpoint: when a gateway or proxy sits in the path, dst_endpoint identifies the gateway that was contacted, while this attribute identifies the logical server that actually served the primitive behind it. For stdio-transported servers there is no network endpoint at all, and this attribute is the only record of the serving system.

source.caption: Source
source.description: The tool source, normalized to the caption of source_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

source_id.caption: Source ID
source_id.description: The normalized identifier of the mechanism through which the capability was provided to the AI system. Orthogonal to type_id, which is the kind of primitive: a Tool may be sourced via MCP, via framework-native function calling, or as a model provider's built-in. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source and carried by the source attribute.

task_uid.caption: Task UID
task_uid.description: The task handle returned for a long-running invocation, per the MCP Tasks extension. Correlates the originating call with subsequent task lifecycle events (get, update, cancel) so an asynchronous tool invocation remains a single thread of activity across events.

transaction_uid.caption: Transaction UID
transaction_uid.description: The capability-layer invocation identifier that correlates a request with its result across events - for MCP, the JSON-RPC request id of the call. Distinct from api.request.uid, which is transport-scoped, and from uid, which identifies the capability itself rather than an invocation of it.

transport.caption: Transport
transport.description: The transport, normalized to the caption of transport_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

transport_id.caption: Transport ID
transport_id.description: The normalized identifier of the transport binding the client used to reach the serving system. Distinguishes a local subprocess server from a remote networked server - a real trust boundary, and the reason an event's network endpoint attributes may legitimately be absent (a stdio server has no network endpoint). Not an IP-layer protocol: protocol_name does not apply, and stdio is not a network protocol at all.

type.caption: Capability Type
type.description: The kind of capability primitive, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Capability Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the kind of capability primitive, per the Model Context Protocol primitive taxonomy. The three primitives carry different risk profiles; a first-class discriminator makes questions like "resource reads vs. tool calls" queryable rather than buried in free-text operation names.

uri.caption: URI
uri.description: The URI of the capability. For Resource primitives this is the resource URI that was read, e.g. file:///project/README.md.

version.caption: AI Capability Version
version.description: The version of the capability as advertised by its provider, when versioned.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable model name. For example: gpt-4o, claude-3-sonnet, or text-embedding-ada-002.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the AI model.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_provider.caption: AI Provider
ai_provider.description: AI service provider or organization name. For example: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Internal.

version.caption: Version
version.description: Model version identifier. For example: 2024-05-13, v2.1.0, or beta.

stop_reason.caption: Stop Reason
stop_reason.description: The reason the model completion ended, as reported by the event source. Normalized to the caption of the stop_reason_id value (e.g. Token Limit); when the value is 'Other', this carries the event source's native label (e.g. recitation, malformed_function_call).

stop_reason_id.caption: Stop Reason ID
stop_reason_id.description: The normalized reason the model completion ended. Producers map their runtime's native value into this set. Populate on completion events; when the value is 'Other', set stop_reason to the event source's native label. Because completion behavior is bound to the configuration that produced it, a shift in this attribute's distribution is more meaningful when weighed against that configuration: ai_model.version for direct model invocations, and ai_agent.version, ai_agent.charter, and ai_agent.instance_uid for agent-mediated operations.

permission_result.caption: Permission Result
permission_result.description: The outcome of the agent runtime's permission check for this operation, as reported by the runtime. Normalized to the caption of the permission_result_id value; when the value is 'Other', this carries the runtime's native label.

permission_result_id.caption: Permission Result ID
permission_result_id.description: The normalized outcome of the agent runtime's permission check for this operation, as reported by the runtime. Producers map their runtime's native value into this set; when the value is 'Other', set permission_result to the runtime's native label.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The information pertaining to the API group.

request.caption: API Request Details
request.description: Details pertaining to the API request.

response.caption: API Response Details
response.description: Details pertaining to the API response.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The information pertaining to the API service.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The API or client token used to authenticate or authorize the API request. This attribute contains the base token object that represents: (1) IdP-issued client tokens (type_id: 6) such as Okta API tokens or Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, or (2) generic API tokens/keys (type_id: 7) used for SaaS application authentication. Use this attribute when the API request was authenticated using a token that should be tracked as part of the API activity event. Note: Protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) should be represented using authentication_token in authentication events, not in API activity events.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the API service.

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The Mitigation object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

sub_technique.caption: MITRE Sub-technique
sub_technique.description: The Sub-technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Sub-technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactic.caption: MITRE Tactic
tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the Tactic ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactics.caption: Tactics
tactics.description: The Tactics associated with the attack technique.

technique.caption: MITRE Technique
technique.description: The Technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Matrix version.

authority_uid.caption: Authority ID
authority_uid.description: Unique identifier of the authority that produced this attestation. When the attestation has a signature, authority_uid ties the signing credential to a known party: because signing credentials rotate and expire, a verifier uses this identifier to confirm that the credential belongs to the expected authority, rather than to a different holder of some otherwise-valid credential. Where multiple signatures are present, it identifies the authority that produced the attestation; the identity of each co-signer is carried within its own digital_signature object. Included in the canonical serialization.

chain_uid.caption: Chain ID
chain_uid.description: Identifier of the append-only chain, such as a forensic or audit log, that this event belongs to. It groups a sequence of attestations so that an independent verifier can locate and validate them in order; it identifies the chain itself and is not a reference to any event outside of this one. Stable for the lifetime of the chain. For example, every attestation produced during a single agent session shares one chain_uid, so querying events whose attestation.chain_uid matches retrieves the full chain, including its newest entry, while each event links to its predecessor through prev_event.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of this event's canonical serialization. If signatures are present, each signature is computed over this fingerprint. Without signatures, the fingerprint alone still detects accidental alteration or corruption of the event. The next event in a chain references this value through its own prev_event.fingerprint.

prev_event.caption: Previous Event
prev_event.description: Reference to the previous event in a tamper-evident chain, carrying that event's fingerprint together with locator attributes for retrieval. Absent on the first, or genesis, event of a chain.

signatures.caption: Digital Signatures
signatures.description: One or more digital signatures, each computed over this event's fingerprint and thereby over the event's canonical serialization, each bound to a verifiable identity. The first entry is typically the producer; additional entries carry co-signatures such as a notary or witness over the same event. The signing algorithm, certificate or public-key material, and signing time are carried within each digital_signature object.

uid.caption: Attestation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of this attestation. It distinguishes an individual attestation, such as a single entry within a tamper-evident chain, from the chain as a whole. See chain_uid for the identifier of the chain itself.

device.caption: Device
device.description: Device used to complete an authentication request.

email_addr.caption: Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address used in an email-based authentication factor.

factor_type.caption: Factor Type
factor_type.description: The type of authentication factor used in an authentication attempt.

factor_type_id.caption: Factor Type ID
factor_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the authentication factor.

is_hotp.caption: HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP)
is_hotp.description: Whether the authentication factor is an HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP).

is_totp.caption: Time-based One-time Password (TOTP)
is_totp.description: Whether the authentication factor is a Time-based One-time Password (TOTP).

phone_number.caption: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone number used for a telephony-based authentication request.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name of provider for an authentication factor.

security_questions.caption: Security Questions
security_questions.description: The question(s) provided to user for a question-based authentication factor.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time that the authentication token was created or issued. This corresponds to the token issuance time, such as the iat (issued at) claim in OIDC tokens, the issue instant in SAML assertions, or the ticket start time in Kerberos tickets.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the authentication token.

is_renewable.caption: Renewable
is_renewable.description: Indicates whether the authentication token is renewable.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The last time the token was updated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The human-friendly name of a token or key, if available, such as the name from the Okta API Token API.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The unique identifier of the tenant or organization that owns the token or key, or the tenant context in which the token is authorized for use. This is particularly relevant in multi-tenant Identity Provider scenarios where tokens are scoped to specific tenants.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the authentication token.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized authentication token type identifier. This attribute restricts the base token.type_id enum to only protocol-specific authentication token types (values 0, 1-5, 99). API tokens and client tokens (values 6-7) are not valid for authentication_token - use the base token object for those types.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique ID of a token or key, if available, such as the Secret ID of Entra ID Application Registration Client Secrets.

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or geographic region that the token or key is authorized to be used from. This may represent network-based access restrictions, geographic limitations, or other zone-based authorization policies. Examples include Okta's network zone restrictions or cloud provider region restrictions.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the authentication token.

kerberos_flags.caption: Kerberos Flags
kerberos_flags.description: A bitmask, either in hexadecimal or decimal form, which encodes various attributes or permissions associated with a Kerberos ticket. These flags delineate specific characteristics of the ticket, such as its renewability or forwardability.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time that the authentication token was created or issued. This corresponds to the token issuance time, such as the iat (issued at) claim in OIDC tokens, the issue instant in SAML assertions, or the ticket start time in Kerberos tickets.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration time of the authentication token.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The last time the token was updated.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the Identity/Access management policies that are applicable.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the certificate was created.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the certificate.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: The fingerprint list of the certificate.

is_self_signed.caption: Certificate Self-Signed
is_self_signed.description: Denotes whether a digital certificate is self-signed or signed by a known certificate authority (CA).

sans.caption: Subject Alternative Names
sans.description: The list of subject alternative names that are secured by a specific certificate.

serial_number.caption: Certificate Serial Number
serial_number.description: The serial number of the certificate used to create the digital signature.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the certificate.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the certificate was created.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration time of the certificate.

account.caption: Account
account.description:
The Account object containing details about the cloud account, subscription, or billing unit where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the account name, unique identifier, type, labels, and tags.

Examples:
  • AWS: Account object with name, uid (Account ID), type, and other account properties
  • Azure: Subscription object with name, uid (Subscription ID), type, and subscription metadata
  • GCP: Project object with name, uid (Project ID), type, and project attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Compartment object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and compartment details

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description:
The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the event or finding was created, often used for compliance, governance, or regional separation.

Examples:
  • AWS: Partition where the event occurred (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov)
  • Azure: Cloud environment where the event occurred (AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment, AzureChinaCloud)

org.caption: Organization
org.description:
The Organization object containing details about the organizational unit or management structure that governs the account, subscription, or project where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the organization name, unique identifier, type, and other organizational metadata.

Examples:
  • AWS: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and other organizational properties
  • Azure: Management Group object with name, uid (Management Group ID), type, and management group metadata
  • GCP: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and organizational attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Tenancy object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and tenancy details

project_uid.caption: Project ID
project_uid.description: The unique identifier of a Cloud project.

provider.caption: Cloud Provider
provider.description: The unique name of the Cloud services provider where the event or finding was created. Examples include AWS, Azure, GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, or other public, private, or hybrid cloud providers.

region.caption: Region
region.description:
The cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Region where the event occurred (us-east-1, eu-west-1)
  • Azure: Region where the event occurred (East US, West Europe)
  • GCP: Region where the event occurred (us-central1, europe-west1)
  • Oracle Cloud: Region where the event occurred (us-ashburn-1, uk-london-1)

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description:
The availability zone in the cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-east-1a, us-east-1b)
  • Azure: Availability zone where the event occurred (1, 2, 3 within a region)
  • GCP: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-central1-a, us-central1-b)
  • Oracle Cloud: Availability zone where the event occurred (AD-1, AD-2, AD-3)

audience.caption: Audience
audience.description: The service or resource this delegation may be exercised against - the relying party that should accept it, and that should reject it if presented anywhere else. When the delegation is carried by an issued token, this is the audience the token names, typically a URI or service identifier for the relying party. The issuer populates it at delegation time from the grant it minted, so an issuer that scopes a delegation to a particular relying party already holds the value; issuers that mint unscoped delegations omit it, which is why the attribute is optional. Note this is the party the authority is exercised on, not the party that later reads or audits the record - a delegation restricted to one payments API keeps that restriction on record regardless of who consumes the event afterwards.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the delegation was issued by the issuing authority.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The time when this delegation's granted authority expires. After this time the delegation no longer conveys authority, independent of any revocation.

issuer_uid.caption: Issuer ID
issuer_uid.description: The unique identifier of the trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, orchestration gateway, or SDK wrapper) that generated this delegation. Enables verification that delegation IDs were issued by an authorized component rather than self-asserted by the delegate.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Delegation ID
parent_uid.description: The delegation identifier of the parent delegation, if this delegation was created by re-delegating authority to another party (e.g., a downstream service or automated process). This creates a parent-child relationship that enables tracking the complete chain of delegation ancestry. Does not indicate that the delegate was instantiated or spawned by the parent's delegate; that relationship, if any, is tracked separately.

scopes.caption: Scopes
scopes.description: The authorization scopes granted at this delegation node, bounding what the delegate is authorized to do on the principal's behalf (e.g., OAuth scope labels). Comparing a delegation's scopes with its parent's scopes reveals scope attenuation across the chain.

uid.caption: Delegation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier for this delegation context. Must be stable across the lifetime of the delegation and generated by a trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, or orchestration gateway) rather than self-asserted by the delegate. All events executed under this delegation share this identifier.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the delegation was issued by the issuing authority.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The time when this delegation's granted authority expires. After this time the delegation no longer conveys authority, independent of any revocation.

name.caption: Name
name.description:
The alternate device name, ordinarily as assigned by an administrator.

Note: The Name could be any other string that helps to identify the device, such as a phone number; for example 310-555-1234.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the device. For example the Windows TargetSID or AWS EC2 ARN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The network domain where the device resides. For example: work.example.com.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The device IP address, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the device.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The device type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

autoscale_uid.caption: Autoscale UID
autoscale_uid.description: The unique identifier of the cloud autoscale configuration.

boot_time.caption: Boot Time
boot_time.description: The time the system was booted.

boot_uid.caption: Boot UID
boot_uid.description: A unique identifier of the device that changes after every reboot. For example, the value of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id from Linux's procfs.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the device, ordinarily as reported by the operating system.

eid.caption: EID
eid.description: An Embedded Identity Document, is a unique serial number that identifies an eSIM-enabled device.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The group names to which the device belongs. For example: ["Windows Laptops", "Engineering"].

hypervisor.caption: Hypervisor
hypervisor.description: The name of the hypervisor running on the device. For example, Xen, VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox, etc.

iccid.caption: ICCID
iccid.description: The Integrated Circuit Card Identification of a mobile device. Typically it is a unique 18 to 22 digit number that identifies a SIM card.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The image used as a template to run the virtual machine.

imei.caption: IMEI
imei.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity that is associated with the device.

imei_list.caption: IMEI List
imei_list.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity values that are associated with the device.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

is_compliant.caption: Compliant Device
is_compliant.description: The event occurred on a compliant device.

is_managed.caption: Managed Device
is_managed.description: The event occurred on a managed device.

is_mobile_account_active.caption: Mobile Account Active
is_mobile_account_active.description: Indicates whether the device has an active mobile account. For example, this is indicated by the itunesStoreAccountActive value within JAMF Pro mobile devices.

is_personal.caption: Personal Device
is_personal.description: The event occurred on a personal device.

is_shared.caption: Shared Device
is_shared.description: The event occurred on a shared device.

is_supervised.caption: Supervised Device
is_supervised.description: The event occurred on a supervised device. Devices that are supervised are typically mobile devices managed by a Mobile Device Management solution and are restricted from specific behaviors such as Apple AirDrop.

is_trusted.caption: Trusted Device
is_trusted.description: The event occurred on a trusted device.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

meid.caption: MEID
meid.description: The Mobile Equipment Identifier. It's a unique number that identifies a Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) mobile device.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model of the device. For example ThinkPad X1 Carbon.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the device was last known to have been modified.

network_interfaces.caption: Network Interfaces
network_interfaces.description:
The physical or virtual network interfaces that are associated with the device, one for each unique MAC address/IP address/hostname/name combination.

Note: The first element of the array is the network information that pertains to the event.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the device.

os_machine_uuid.caption: OS Machine UUID
os_machine_uuid.description: The operating system assigned Machine ID. In Windows, this is the value stored at the registry path: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid. In Linux, this is stored in the file: /etc/machine-id.

peripheral_devices.caption: Peripheral Device
peripheral_devices.description: The peripheral devices that are attached or connected to the device.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The region where the virtual machine is located. For example, an AWS Region.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

udid.caption: Unique Device Identifier
udid.description: The Apple assigned Unique Device Identifier (UDID). For iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS devices, this is the UDID. For macOS devices, it is the Provisioning UDID. For example: 00008020-008D4548007B4F26

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: An alternate unique identifier of the device if any. For example the ActiveDirectory DN.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor for the device. For example Dell or Lenovo.

boot_time_dt.caption: Boot Time
boot_time_dt.description: The time the system was booted.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

first_seen_time_dt.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time_dt.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

last_seen_time_dt.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time_dt.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the device was last known to have been modified.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The enrichment data associated with the attribute and value. The meaning of this data depends on the type the enrichment record.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A long description of the enrichment data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: The reputation of the enrichment data.

short_desc.caption: Short Description
short_desc.description: A short description of the enrichment data.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL of the source of the enrichment data.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The algorithm or scheme used to create the fingerprint, normalized to the caption of algorithm_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized algorithm or scheme, which was used to create the fingerprint.

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The encoding of the value attribute, normalized to the caption of encoding_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding used to represent the fingerprint bytes as the string in value. A verifier must decode value using this encoding to recover the raw hash bytes.

serialization.caption: Serialization
serialization.description: The canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

serialization_id.caption: Serialization ID
serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the fingerprinted input. Use Flat where the fingerprinted data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were hashed.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The fingerprint value.

Note: This uses type file_hash_t ("Hash"), which has been generalized for all fingerprints but retains the same name and caption for backwards compatibility.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

condition.caption: Condition
condition.description: The rule trigger condition for the rule. For example: SQL_INJECTION.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The rule response time duration, usually used for challenge completion time.

match_details.caption: Match Details
match_details.description: The data in a request that rule matched. For example: '["10","and","1"]'.

match_location.caption: Match Location
match_location.description: The location of the matched data in the source which resulted in the triggered firewall rule. For example: HEADER.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: The rate limit for a rate-based rule.

sensitivity.caption: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: The sensitivity of the firewall rule in the matched event. For example: HIGH.

args.caption: HTTP Arguments
args.description: The arguments sent along with the HTTP request.

body_length.caption: Request Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP request body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

http_method.caption: HTTP Method
http_method.description: The HTTP request method indicates the desired action to be performed for a given resource.

length.caption: Request Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP request, in number of bytes.

referrer.caption: HTTP Referrer
referrer.description: The request header that identifies the address of the previous web page, which is linked to the current web page or resource being requested.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the http request.

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL object that pertains to the request.

user_agent.caption: HTTP User-Agent
user_agent.description: The request header that identifies the operating system and web browser.

x_forwarded_for.caption: X-Forwarded-For
x_forwarded_for.description: The X-Forwarded-For header identifying the originating IP address(es) of a client connecting to a web server through an HTTP proxy or a load balancer.

body_length.caption: Response Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP response body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) status code returned from the web server to the client. For example, 200.

content_type.caption: HTTP Content Type
content_type.description: The HTTP request header that identifies the original media type of the resource (prior to any content encoding applied for sending).

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

latency.caption: Latency
latency.description: The HTTP response latency measured in milliseconds.

length.caption: Response Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP response, in number of bytes.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The HTTP status code and reason phrase returned from the server.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The response status. For example: A successful HTTP status of 'OK' which corresponds to a code of 200.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The malware name, as reported by the detection engine.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the specific malware instance, as assigned by the detection engine (e.g., virus signature ID or IPS rule ID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

classification_ids.caption: Classification IDs
classification_ids.description: The list of normalized identifiers of the malware classifications.

classifications.caption: Classifications
classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

cves.caption: CVE List
cves.description: The list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers associated with the malware.

files.caption: Files
files.description: The list of file objects representing files that were identified as infected by the malware.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The number of files that were identified to be infected by the malware.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The filesystem path of the malware that was observed.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name or identifier of the security solution or service that provided the malware detection information.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the malware, normalized to the captions of the severity_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the malware severity.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

uid.caption: Scan UID
uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

num_files.caption: Scanned Files
num_files.description: The total number of files analyzed during the scan.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The total number of files identified as infected with malware during the scan.

num_volumes.caption: Number of Volumes
num_volumes.description: The total number of storage volumes examined during the malware scan.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The total size in bytes of all files that were scanned.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

unique_malware_count.caption: Unique Malware Count
unique_malware_count.description: The number of unique malware detected across all infected files.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name or identifier of the message context. In AI systems, this could be the conversation ID, session name, thread identifier, or interaction name (e.g., 'user-session-123', 'conversation-abc', 'chat-thread-456').

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the message context. This could be a session ID, conversation ID, or other unique identifier that allows correlation of messages within the same context.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_role_id.caption: AI Role ID
ai_role_id.description: Specifies the functional role of the AI within the context of this message, such as retrieving information, assisting reasoning, executing a tool, or generating content.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The initiating client application. In AI systems, this represents the client-side application or framework that initiates requests (e.g., LangChain application, web browser, mobile app, SDK implementation).

completion_tokens.caption: Completion Tokens
completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the model's response/completion for this message.

prompt_text.caption: Prompt Text
prompt_text.description: The text of the input prompt provided to the model for this message. This is the verbatim instruction, query, or context supplied to the AI system that drove the operation.

prompt_tokens.caption: Prompt Tokens
prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the input prompt for this message.

response_text.caption: Response Text
response_text.description: The text of the model's response generated for this message. For agent-mediated operations, this is the content returned by the assistant, tool, or agent.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The server or service handling the request. In AI systems, this represents the AI service, API endpoint, or agent that processes and responds to requests (e.g., OpenAI API service, Claude API service, internal AI model service).

total_tokens.caption: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used for this message (prompt + completion).

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

correlation_uid.caption: Correlation UID
correlation_uid.description: A unique identifier used to correlate this OCSF event with other related OCSF events, distinct from the event's uid value. This enables linking multiple OCSF events that are part of the same activity, transaction, or security incident across different systems or time periods.

debug.caption: Debug Information
debug.description: Debug information about non-fatal issues with this OCSF event. Each issue is a line in this string array.

event_code.caption: Event Code
event_code.description: The identifier of the original event. For example the numerical Windows Event Code or Cisco syslog code.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.caption: Schema Extensions
extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to the event. For example: ["sample", "dev"]

log_facility.caption: Log Facility
log_facility.description: The syslog facility, normalized to the caption of the log_facility_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

log_facility_id.caption: Log Facility ID
log_facility_id.description: The facility of the source syslog message, identifying the originating subsystem that generated it. The facility is independent of severity and is not recoverable from severity_id. A relay may rewrite or regenerate a message, so this reflects the source (original) facility rather than a value guaranteed to be stable across hops, and it should be populated only when the source is syslog or an equivalent facility mapping is unambiguous. There is no Unknown value: 0 is the kernel (kern) facility, so an absent or malformed PRI must not be mapped to 0; use 99 (Other) for a known nonstandard or source-defined facility.

log_format.caption: Log Source Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log where the data originated. For example CSV, XML, Windows Multiline, JSON, syslog or Cisco Log Schema.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The event log name, typically for the consumer of the event. For example, the storage bucket name, SIEM repository index name, etc.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example AWS CloudWatch or Splunk.

log_source.caption: Log Source
log_source.description: The log system or component where the data originated. For example, a file path, syslog server name or a Windows hostname and logging subsystem such as Security.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

loggers.caption: Loggers
loggers.description: An ordered array of Logger objects describing each hop in the event pipeline between the source and its final destination. Each entry captures the logging product, device, and timestamps (logged_time, transmit_time) at that stage. The last entry's logged_time should match metadata.logged_time.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_event_uid.caption: Original Event ID
original_event_uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the event in its original logging system before transformation to OCSF format. This field preserves the source system's native event identifier, enabling traceability back to the raw log entry. For example, a Windows Event Record ID, a syslog message ID, a Splunk _cd value, or a database transaction log sequence number.

original_time.caption: Original Time
original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source, preserved as a pass-through string in its native format (e.g., Syslog timestamp, Windows event time). This is not normalized to timestamp_t - the normalized equivalent is the base event time attribute. Omit if the event is generated rather than collected via logs.

processed_time.caption: Processed Time
processed_time.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.caption: Profiles
profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

reporter.caption: Reporter
reporter.description: The entity from which the event or finding was first reported.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.
