source.caption: Source
source.description: The source of the event or finding. This can be any distinguishing name for the logical origin of the data — for example, 'CloudTrail Events', or a use case like 'Attack Simulations' or 'Vulnerability Scans'.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the event.

total_queued_duration.caption: Total Queued Duration
total_queued_duration.description: The amount of time an event spent in a queue awaiting processing. In this case, the value is the difference between processed_time and logged_time. This duration is inclusive of all queues between the originator of the event and the intended long-term storage destination of the event.

transformation_info_list.caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info_list.description: An array of transformation info that describes the mappings or transforms applied to the data.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the event or finding as a subset of the source of the event. This can be any distinguishing characteristic of the data. For example 'Management Events' or 'Device Penetration Test'.

uid.caption: Event UID
uid.description: A unique identifier assigned to the OCSF event. This ID is specific to the OCSF event itself and is distinct from the original event identifier in the source system (see original_event_uid).

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

logged_time_dt.caption: Logged Time
logged_time_dt.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

processed_time_dt.caption: Processed Time
processed_time_dt.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

transmit_time_dt.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time_dt.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: Fingerprints that identify the specific application implementation on this endpoint, such as Cisco NPF or HASSH.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

network_scope.caption: Network Scope
network_scope.description: Indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined. The value is normalized to the caption of the network_scope_id.

network_scope_id.caption: Network Scope ID
network_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the endpoint’s network scope. The normalized network scope identifier indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined.

port.caption: Port
port.description: The port used for communication within the network connection.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The network proxy information pertaining to a specific endpoint. This can be used to describe information pertaining to network address translation (NAT).

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

wifi.caption: Wireless Network
wifi.description: The wireless network that this endpoint is associated with, or that this endpoint advertises when it is an access point.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier (metadata.uid) of the source OCSF event from which this observable was extracted. This field enables linking observables back to their originating event data when observables are stored in a separate location or system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The full name of the observable attribute. The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name. Array attributes may be represented in one of three ways. For example: resources.uid, resources[].uid, resources[0].uid.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Contains the original and normalized reputation scores.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The OCSF event type UID (type_uid) of the source event that this observable was extracted from. This field enables filtering and categorizing observables by their originating event type. For example: 400101 for Network Activity (class_uid 4001) with activity_id 1.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The value associated with the observable attribute. The meaning of the value depends on the observable type.
If the name refers to a scalar attribute, then the value is the value of the attribute.
If the name refers to an object attribute, then the value is not populated.

answers.caption: Related DNS Answers
answers.description: Any pertinent DNS answers information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: MITRE ATT&CK Tactics, Techniques, and/or Procedures (TTPs) pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: Any pertinent autonomous system information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

campaign.caption: Campaign
campaign.description: The campaign object describes details about the campaign that was the source of the activity.

category.caption: Category
category.description: Categorizes the threat indicator based on its functional or operational role.

comment.caption: Analyst Comments
comment.description: Analyst commentary or source commentary about an indicator or OSINT analysis.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence of an indicator or analysis, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source or analyst.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized identifier of the confidence level, reflecting the accuracy or pertinence of the OSINT indicator or analysis. A low confidence indicates that the collected information lacked sufficient detail or accuracy to fully qualify the indicator as malicious. When the value is 99 (Other), the confidence attribute must contain the source-specific label.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the indicator was initially created or identified.

creator.caption: Creator
creator.description: The identifier of the user, system, or organization that contributed the indicator.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A detailed explanation of the indicator, including its context, purpose, and relevance.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: The specific detection pattern or signature associated with the indicator.

detection_pattern_type.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern_type.description: The detection pattern type, normalized to the caption of the detection_pattern_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

detection_pattern_type_id.caption: Detection Pattern Type ID
detection_pattern_type_id.description: Specifies the type of detection pattern used to identify the associated threat indicator.

email.caption: Related Email
email.description: Any email information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

email_auth.caption: Related Email Authentication
email_auth.description: Any email authentication information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration date of the indicator, after which it is no longer considered reliable.

external_uid.caption: External ID
external_uid.description: A unique identifier assigned by an external system for cross-referencing.

file.caption: Related File
file.description: Any pertinent file information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

intrusion_sets.caption: Intrusion Sets
intrusion_sets.description: A grouping of adversarial behaviors and resources believed to be associated with specific threat actors or campaigns. Intrusion sets often encompass multiple campaigns and are used to organize related activities under a common label.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: Lockheed Martin Kill Chain Phases pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: Tags or keywords associated with the indicator to enhance searchability.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: Any pertinent geolocation information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp of the last modification or update to the indicator.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name.

references.caption: References
references.description: Provides a reference to an external source of information related to the CTI being represented. This may include a URL, a document, or some other type of reference that provides additional context or information about the CTI.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Any analytics related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Related reputational analysis from third-party engines and analysts for a given indicator or OSINT analysis.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: A numerical representation of the threat indicator’s risk level.

script.caption: Related Script Data
script.description: Any pertinent script information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: Represents the severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

signatures.caption: Related Digital Signatures
signatures.description: Any digital signatures or hashes related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL of an indicator or OSINT analysis, e.g., a URL back to a TIP, report, or otherwise.

subdomains.caption: Related Subdomains
subdomains.description: Any pertinent subdomain information - such as those generated by a Domain Generation Algorithm - related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

subnet.caption: Related Subnet
subnet.description: A CIDR or network block related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

threat_actor.caption: Threat Actor
threat_actor.description: A threat actor is an individual or group that conducts malicious cyber activities, often with financial, political, or ideological motives.

tlp.caption: Traffic Light Protocol
tlp.description: The Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) was created to facilitate greater sharing of potentially sensitive information and more effective collaboration. TLP provides a simple and intuitive schema for indicating with whom potentially sensitive information can be shared.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the OSINT object.

uploaded_time.caption: Uploaded Time
uploaded_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the associated indicator or intelligence was added to the system or repository.

value.caption: Indicator
value.description: The actual indicator value in scope, e.g., a SHA-256 hash hexdigest or a domain name.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor name of a tool which generates intelligence or provides indicators.

vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Any vulnerabilities related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

whois.caption: WHOIS
whois.description: Any pertinent WHOIS information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the indicator was initially created or identified.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration date of the indicator, after which it is no longer considered reliable.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The timestamp of the last modification or update to the indicator.

uploaded_time_dt.caption: Uploaded Time
uploaded_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the associated indicator or intelligence was added to the system or repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The policy name. For example: AdministratorAccess Policy.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier of the policy instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the policy such as the underlying JSON policy itself or other details.

is_applied.caption: Applied
is_applied.description: A determination if the content of a policy was applied to a target or request, or not.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The policy type. For example: Identity Policy, Resource Policy, Service Control Policy, etc..

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

cpid.caption: Common Process Identifier
cpid.description: A unique process identifier that can be assigned deterministically by multiple system data producers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that this process is running or hosting, if applicable. Populate when the process serves as the runtime environment for an AI agent (e.g., a Python process executing a LangChain agent or hosting an MCP server). When a process hosts multiple agents and the activity cannot be attributed to one specifically, use hosted_ai_agent_list instead.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

environment_variables.caption: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: Environment variables associated with the process.

hosted_ai_agent_list.caption: Hosted AI Agent List
hosted_ai_agent_list.description: The list of autonomous AI agents hosted by this process. Use when a single process hosts multiple agents (e.g., an IDE running several coding agents within the same host process) and the producer cannot attribute a specific activity to a single agent. When attribution is available, populate the singular ai_agent attribute instead.

integrity.caption: Integrity
integrity.description: The process integrity level, normalized to the caption of the integrity_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source (Windows only).

integrity_id.caption: Integrity Level
integrity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the process integrity level (Windows only).

lineage.caption: Lineage
lineage.description: The lineage of the process, represented by a list of paths for each ancestor process. For example: ['/usr/sbin/sshd', '/usr/bin/bash', '/usr/bin/whoami'].

loaded_modules.caption: Loaded Modules
loaded_modules.description: The list of loaded module names.

parent_process.caption: Parent Process
parent_process.description: The parent process of this process object. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object, to prevent deep nesting. Additional ancestry information can be supplied in the ancestry attribute.

ptid.caption: Process Thread ID
ptid.description: The identifier of the process thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

sandbox.caption: Sandbox
sandbox.description: The name of the containment jail (i.e., sandbox). For example, hardened_ps, high_security_ps, oracle_ps, netsvcs_ps, or default_ps.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session under which this process is running.

terminated_time.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time.description: The time when the process was terminated.

tid.caption: Thread ID
tid.description: The identifier of the thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user under which this process is running.

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: The working directory of a process.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description:
An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs that represent a process extended attribute.

For example: process security context attributes, process resource limits, container-specific attributes, or platform-specific process metadata not covered by standard OCSF attributes.

auid.caption: Audit User ID
auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

egid.caption: Effective Group ID
egid.description: The effective group under which this process is running.

euid.caption: Effective User ID
euid.description: The effective user under which this process is running.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The group under which this process is running.

hosted_services.caption: Hosted Services
hosted_services.description: The Windows services that this process is hosting.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the process was created/started.

terminated_time_dt.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time_dt.description: The time when the process was terminated.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the service.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated with the service.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the service.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of identical sessions spawned from the same source IP, destination IP, application, and content/threat type seen over a period of time.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the session was created.

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

expiration_reason.caption: Expiration Reason
expiration_reason.description: The reason which triggered the session expiration.

is_mfa.caption: Multi Factor Authentication
is_mfa.description: Indicates whether Multi Factor Authentication was used during authentication.

is_remote.caption: Remote
is_remote.description: The indication of whether the session is remote.

is_vpn.caption: VPN Session
is_vpn.description: The indication of whether the session is a VPN session.

issuer.caption: Issuer Details
issuer.description: The identifier of the session issuer.

terminal.caption: Terminal
terminal.description: The Pseudo Terminal associated with the session. Ex: the tty or pts value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the session.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate unique identifier of the session. e.g. AWS ARN - arn:aws:sts::123344444444:assumed-role/Admin/example-session.

uuid.caption: UUID
uuid.description: The universally unique identifier of the session.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the session was created.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique user identifier. For example, the Windows user SID, ActiveDirectory DN or AWS user ARN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The user's account or the account associated with the user.

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the user, as reported by the product.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the user is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

full_name.caption: Full Name
full_name.description: The full name of the user, as reported by the product.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The administrative groups to which the user belongs.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Assigned
has_mfa.description: The user has a multi-factor or secondary-factor device assigned.

ldap_person.caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the user.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Details about the programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated to the user.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the user. For example, System, AWS IAM User, etc.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory user GUID or AWS user Principal ID.
